out.name: Combat Reflexes

out.name: Danger Sense

out.name: Hard to Subdue

Receive help from authorities when in minor legal trouble or when caught using Beyonder powers without harm to innocents. Earn contribution points for important information or assistance, exchangeable for money or Beyonder formulas/ingredients. 5 pts: newly recruited, must prove your worth. 10–15 pts: trusted informant; the organisation's representative trusts your judgement.

Benefits: Spirit Vision (see Chapter 4: Universal Beyonder Ability — Spirit Vision), Revolver +2, Ritualistic Magic +1, Hidden Lore (Beyonders) +3, Occultism +2, Hermes Language (Broken). out.name: Versatile

out.name: Intuition
out.notes: Once per session, the GM may give you a meaningful hunch about a decision. Ask the GM: 'Is this a good/bad idea?' The GM must answer honestly.

out.name: Lightning Calculator

out.name: Absolute Direction

out.name: Acute Social Awareness

out.name: Class Mobility
out.notes: Move believably across two social classes. +2 to Savoir-Faire in either; NPCs rarely question your presence.

out.name: Connections: Church Lay Staff
out.notes: Recognized civilian assistant to one Orthodox Church. Access to facilities; some protection from routine Nighthawk scrutiny.

out.name: Connections: Press Credentials
out.notes: Recognized press identity. Opens doors otherwise closed; plausible reason to be anywhere in a city.

out.name: Fearsome Reputation
out.notes: Known in criminal circles. Relevant NPCs start cautious; Intimidation in these circles is at +2.

out.name: Falsified Identity
out.notes: A fully documented second identity in official records, distinct from your real one. Holds under regular police scrutiny and superficial investigation; fails if an investigator or official Beyonder peers deeper. Requires arranging papers (see Hired Allies & Services).

out.name: Local Legend
out.notes: Well-known in one neighbourhood (specify). +2 to social rolls there; people look out for you.

out.name: Mentor
out.notes: Senior figure offers intermittent guidance. Once per session consult for info, a contact, or a skill roll at their level.

out.name: Multilingual
out.notes: Fluent in two additional languages. No penalty to language-dependent social skills in those languages.

out.name: Natural Leader
out.notes: When you issue a direct command under pressure, allies may reroll their first Fright Check or morale roll with +1. Once per scene.

out.name: Police Informant
out.notes: Arrangement with local constabulary. Minor legal trouble can often be redirected. Discreet — exposure would be dangerous.

out.name: Respectable Address
out.notes: Lodgings in a creditable neighbourhood. +1 to social rolls with middle/upper class NPCs who would otherwise look down on you.

out.name: Street Credibility
out.notes: Trusted in the working-class underground. Call in small favours from dock workers, factory hands, and street operators once per session.

out.name: Fearlessness
out.notes: +1 per level to Fright Checks; also grants immunity to intimidation from beings with fewer levels of Fearlessness than you. Vital in a world of horrors.

out.name: Fit
out.notes: +1 to all HT rolls; Allows you to Burn FP during combat.

out.name: Very Fit
out.notes: +2 to all HT rolls; recover FP at twice the normal rate. Prerequisite: Fit. Allows you to Burn FP during combat and out of combat.

out.name: Wealth: Comfortable
out.notes: Good income; start with £5. Status 1 — those impressed by wealth treat you better (GM discretion).

out.name: Hunting License
out.notes: Legal in Loen for hunting rifle only. Costs £5 to obtain in-game. Valid in rural/suburban areas — carrying in city limits draws police attention.

out.name: General Weapon Certificate
out.notes: Full civilian firearm permit. Costs £50 to obtain in-game. Allows carry of any non-military weapon in cities; required for pistols, rifles, shotguns in urban areas.

out.name: Legal Enforcement Powers
out.notes: Official authority to investigate, detain, and carry weapons in the line of duty. Works within jurisdiction only; may vary by city or organization.

out.name: Black Market Access
out.notes: Reliable source for illegal or restricted goods. Once per session attempt to acquire a specific item outside legal channels.

out.name: Experienced Investigator
out.notes: Once per investigation scene ask the GM one yes/no question about observable evidence without a skill roll.

out.name: Former Military Officer
out.notes: Leadership and Tactics at +1; military contacts; entitled to officer courtesies in formal settings.

out.name: Industrial Expertise
out.notes: Deep familiarity with a specific industry (specify). +2 to all relevant skill rolls; NPCs in that industry trust your knowledge.

out.name: Medical Training (Informal)
out.notes: Use Physician at IQ-2 without purchasing the skill; First Aid rolls gain +1.

out.name: Navigator's Eye
out.notes: Never become lost in any city previously visited; rural navigation rolls at +2.

out.name: Photographic Instinct
out.notes: Photography rolls at +2; instinctively know what to capture as evidence.

out.name: Safecracker
out.notes: +3 to Lockpicking for combination locks and mechanical safes specifically.

out.name: Underworld Lawyer
out.notes: Once per session cite an obscure legal technicality convincingly enough to delay, redirect, or dismiss a legal problem.

out.name: Alcohol Tolerance
out.notes: Never suffer social penalties from moderate drinking; Carousing rolls to appear sober at +3.

out.name: Cold Resistance
out.notes: No penalties from cold weather up to freezing; hypothermia rolls at +2.

out.name: Controlled Breathing
out.notes: Hold breath for HT × 3 seconds without a roll; HT rolls to resist airborne toxins at +2.

out.name: Fast Healer
out.notes: Recover 1 additional HP per day of rest. Injuries that would leave others bedridden leave you functional in half the time.

out.name: Hard Stomach
out.notes: No HT rolls required for disgusting environments — gore, corpses, foul conditions.

out.name: Iron Jaw
out.notes: Knockdown rolls from blows to the head at +2; never bite through your own tongue under shock.

out.name: Light Sleeper
out.notes: Perception rolls while sleeping at +4; never caught completely unaware at night.

out.name: Low-Profile Build
out.notes: Physical appearance is unremarkable. All attempts to identify you from description are at -2.

out.name: Night Eyes
out.notes: Reduce all darkness penalties by 2; in dim gaslight or moonlight suffer no penalty at all.

out.name: Perfect Balance
out.notes: +6 to avoid knockdown; +2 to Acrobatics, Climbing, Piloting

out.name: Great Balance
out.notes: +2 to avoid knockdown; +1 to Acrobatics, Climbing, Piloting

out.name: Rapid Recovery
out.notes: Stun durations halved; recover from knockdown in half normal time.

out.name: Flexibility
out.notes: +3 to Climbing and Escape; ignore up to -3 close-quarters penalties.

out.name: Double-Jointed
out.notes: +5 to Climbing and Escape; ignore up to -5 close-quarters penalties for wrestling or grappling; any body part bends any way.

out.name: Acute Vision
out.notes: +2 to Vision rolls; notice details at a distance, read lips, spot hidden objects.

out.name: Incisive Vision
out.notes: Prerequisite: Acute Vision. +4 to all Vision rolls.

out.name: Acute Hearing
out.notes: +2 to Hearing rolls; detect faint sounds, eavesdrop through walls, identify speech in noise.

out.name: Resistant (specify)
out.notes: HT rolls to resist a specific category at +3 (3 pts) or +8 (5 pts). Common choices: Disease, Poison, Temperature Extremes.

out.name: Outdoorsman
out.notes: +1 per level to all Outdoor skills (Camouflage, Fishing, Naturalist, Navigation, Survival, Tracking, Weather Sense). Max 4 levels.

out.name: Aura Sensitivity
out.notes: Sense the emotional weight of places. In locations where violence, grief, or supernatural events occurred, receive a vague impression without rolling.

out.name: Death Sense
out.notes: Passive awareness of recent death within 30 meters (within 24 hours). Sense its direction without rolling; can sense whether a person is dying.

out.name: Divine Touchstone
out.notes: An Orthodox deity has taken minor notice of you. Once per session ask the GM a yes/no question your character senses as an impression.

out.name: Dreamsight
out.notes: Dreams contain genuine information. Once per session the GM may offer a cryptic dream-image related to current events; sharing it grants +1 to one investigation roll.

out.name: Ether Body Awareness
out.notes: Know immediately when a supernatural effect is targeting your soul, not just your body — even without Spirit Vision.

out.name: Fate Sensitivity
out.notes: Once per session when making a decision with major consequences, ask the GM: 'Does this feel wrong?' The GM must answer honestly.

out.name: Ghost Proximity Sense
out.notes: Passive. Sense when a spirit is within 10 meters — a cold certainty. No details; no roll required.

out.name: Pathway Resonance
out.notes: Unexplained affinity with one specific Pathway (specify). +3 to rolls to identify items, individuals, or rituals associated with it.

out.name: Ritual Intuition
out.notes: Sense when a ritual is being performed within 50 meters. Notice the spiritual disturbance without rolling — even without knowing its type.

out.name: Soul Reading (Untrained)
out.notes: Once per scene the GM may offer one true impression about a target's emotional condition or hidden motive. Cannot be triggered deliberately.

out.name: Spirit Vision
out.notes: See the non-physical aspects of beings — Ether Body (health), Spirit Body (emotions), and auras — as well as ghosts and spirits. Activate by expending 1 SPI (see Chapter 4: The Spirituality (SPI) Attribute). May instead be learned in-game from someone who teaches the technique, provided you have a minimum total of 4 SPI.

out.name: Anchored Soul
out.notes: All attempts to alter your mental identity — possession, compulsion, pathway side effects — are at -2 against you.

out.name: Cleansed Spirit
out.notes: CoR gained from passive exposure are halved. Active corruption from deliberate acts is unaffected.

out.name: Cold Iron Tolerance
out.notes: Unaffected by the mild spiritual discomfort iron causes to sensitive individuals. Rare in those with significant spiritual heritage.

out.name: Faithful Grounding
out.notes: Genuine faith acts as an anchor. Fright Checks in church buildings, shrines, or during prayer are at +3.

out.name: Incorruptible Will
out.notes: +3 to all Will rolls to resist Beyonder abilities, evil god whispers, and ritual compulsion. Does not apply to mundane social pressure.

out.name: Spiritual Fortitude
out.notes: Maximum CoR equal Will + 3 rather than just Will.

out.name: Warded Dreams
out.notes: All supernatural attempts to enter, read, or alter your dreams require an additional success by 3 or more to take effect.

out.name: Luck
out.notes: 1 reroll per session — may reroll any one failed roll.

out.name: Beckoning Luck
out.notes: 2 rerolls per session — reroll any failed roll, usable at any time. If the re-roll also fails there is no additional effect — and fate may balance later.

out.name: Born Under a Named Star
out.notes: Seers and Diviners who read your fate always notice something unusual. You register as 'marked' in ways they cannot fully interpret.

out.name: Mystical Item
out.notes: A single mystical item you already possess, defined with the GM. Cost scales with power: a minor charm (5 pts), a useful tool (10 pts), or a significant piece of equipment (15 pts). The item should match one of the 22 pathways' domains. If lost or destroyed, rename this advantage to 'Mystical Item (Lost)' — no refund.

out.name: Charmed Object
out.notes: One item you own provides +1 to one specific skill when used (specify item and skill). Lost permanently if the item is destroyed.

out.name: Dead Language Fluency
out.notes: Read and speak one dead language (Ancient Hermes, Ancient Loen, etc.) without having formally learned it. Origin unexplained.

out.name: Familiar Presence
out.notes: Animals and spirits are unusually calm near you. Domestic animals never startle; non-hostile spirits observe rather than act against you.

out.name: Sequence Knowledge
out.notes: You know the formula for your next Sequence 8 potion — main ingredients, supplementary ingredients, and basic preparation method. This knowledge arrives instinctively once you reach Sequence 9. It does not grant the ingredients, a pre-prepared potion, or an Acting Method. Covers only the immediate next sequence.

out.name: Knows the Acting Method
out.notes: You innately understand the Acting Method for your Pathway. At the end of each session, roll 3d6 — the result is the percentage of digestion progress you gain toward your current potion, in addition to your normal Digestion Gain Per Session.

out.name: Marked by Ritual
out.notes: A lasting spiritual imprint (define with GM). Grants +2 to one type of SPI roll but may attract unusual attention.

out.name: Spirit Tongue
out.notes: Communicate basic intent to ghosts and lingering spirits without the Language of the Dead ability. Limited to yes/no exchanges.

out.name: Uncanny Survivor
out.notes: Once per campaign arc, when you would die on a death roll, succeed automatically instead. The GM decides the cost.

out.name: Sanctity
out.notes: Your connection to the divine is unusually clear. +2 to Theology and Religious Ritual; once per session, the GM must answer one factual question about Church doctrine or history honestly.

out.name: Sequence Advantage
out.text: If the diviner is 2+ Sequences stronger than the target, they ignore the target's passive Sequence penalty (but active techniques like Door Misdirection still apply at half penalty, rounded up).

out.name: Direct Link
out.text: Having the target's true name + an intimate personal item halves all anti-divination penalties (round down).

out.name: HP Sacrifice
out.text: Burning 4+ HP (at 2 HP = 1 SPI rate) when casting a divination ignores -2 of anti-divination penalties for that attempt.

out.name: Anti-Anti-Divination Ritual
out.text: A dedicated ritual (base difficulty -4, requires rare materials worth £100+) can temporarily suppress a target's protective techniques for 1d hours. This requires the target's name and a personal item.

out.name: Divine Intervention
out.text: A prayer to an orthodox deity whose domain includes divination (the God of Knowledge and Wisdom, the Evernight Goddess) may grant a temporary bypass — but the deity will expect something in return. The GM should set a clear cost (a future service, a sacrifice, or a quest) and may limit this to once per story arc.

out.boonLevelRule: Sequence 9 equivalent (+0), Sequence 8 (-2), Sequence 7 (-4), and so on, doubling the penalty with each sequence. Generous sacrifices that align with the patron's domain can offset or even negate this penalty — see Sacrifice quality modifiers above.
consequences: Personality drift: The GM should periodically introduce subtle changes to the character's personality, reflecting the patron's influence. A boon-granted Beyonder of a Fool-adjacent Great One may become more deceptive; one aligned with a Calamity Existence may grow more destructive.
Dreams and visions: The patron may communicate — or simply observe — through the boon connection. Sleep is no longer private.

Increased vulnerability: The connection works both ways. Those with knowledge of the patron may detect the supplicant's taint. Church Inquisitors and Mandated Punishers are trained to recognise boon-granted Beyonders.
Refusal penalty: Once a boon has been accepted, refusing a direct request from the patron may incur spiritual backlash (see Critical Failure Table, Chapter 9, Section V).
requirements: The full honorific name of the Hidden Existence. Incomplete or incorrect names are likely to attract the wrong attention — or no attention at all.

Corresponding mystical ingredients for appeasement. These vary by Great One and are tied to their domain and symbolism. Incense, rare oils, consecrated items, or the blood of specific creatures are common requirements.
A sacrifice. Sacrifices are almost mandatory for even a Sequence 9 equivalent boon. The quality, significance, and appropriateness of the sacrifice directly affect the ritual's outcome.

out.name: Greed

out.name: Overconfidence
out.notes: Believes they can handle situations they cannot

out.name: Bad Temper
out.notes: Must roll vs. 12 to avoid angry outbursts when provoked

out.name: Bully
out.notes: Must roll vs. 12 to resist intimidating or humiliating someone weaker when the opportunity arises

out.name: Obsession
out.notes: Consuming long-term goal dominates life and decisions

out.name: Nightmares
out.notes: Disturbed sleep; wake unrefreshed — lose 1 FP each morning

out.name: Code of Honor
out.notes: Personal code limits actions; must be followed even at cost

out.name: Sense of Duty
out.notes: Must help/protect certain groups even at personal risk

out.name: Social Stigma
out.notes: Society discriminates: Criminal Record -5, Servant Class -5

out.name: Secret
out.notes: Dangerous hidden truth; exposure has severe consequences

out.name: Blacklisted
out.notes: A specific industry, org, or church has your name. Employment or access there fails automatically without disguise.

out.name: Blood Feud
out.notes: A family, gang, or faction holds a grievance. Their agents appear as recurring threats (scale reflects their power).

out.name: Creditor's Target
out.notes: You owe a dangerous debt. Periodic pressure, threats, or interference; cannot ignore it without severe consequences.

out.name: Drafted
out.notes: Technically in a military reserve or conscript pool. Mobilisation orders can arrive at any time, legally compelling service.

out.name: Ex-Convict
out.notes: Social Stigma in formal settings; increased police scrutiny; certain employment and legal protections unavailable.

out.name: Famous Face
out.notes: Recognizable in the city. Disguise attempts at -2; surveillance harder; strangers approach you, sometimes dangerously.

out.name: Fugitive (Minor)
out.notes: Open local warrant on a non-capital charge. Cannot approach police, visit courts, or enter government buildings without risk.

out.name: Fugitive (Serious)
out.notes: Serious criminal charges outstanding. Significant arrest risk on sight in major cities; cannot use real name officially.

out.name: Illegitimate Birth
out.notes: -1 to social rolls in formal/upper-class settings where this is known; inheritance and legal rights are complicated.

out.name: Orphan with Dependents
out.notes: Support younger siblings or a sick relative. Regular financial drain; their safety is a lever enemies can use.

out.name: Refugee Status
out.notes: No legal right of permanent residence. No papers, no safety net; deportation is a real threat; police encounters are dangerous.

out.name: Wanted by Church
out.notes: An Orthodox Church has marked you. Not just the police — Nighthawks or equivalent Beyonder enforcers may be looking.

out.name: Duty (specify)
out.notes: Regular, enforced obligation to an organization or individual. Value reflects frequency and danger: -5 for light duty (roll 6 or less), -10 for hazardous duty (roll 9 or less), -15 for extremely hazardous (roll 12 or less; appears weekly). Specify organization and nature at creation.

out.name: Absent-Mindedness
out.notes: -3 to skill rolls requiring concentration or organisation in everyday life; must roll vs. IQ to remember to do something if interrupted or distracted. In combat, may forget to reload, change tactics, or use special abilities (GM's discretion).

out.name: Addiction (specify)
out.notes: Compulsive dependence on a substance. Value reflects the substance's cost, the severity of its effects, and its legality: cheap legal vices are mild (e.g., Tobacco, -3), costly or mildly illegal habits run about -10 (e.g., Laudanum), and ruinously expensive, dangerous, or strictly illegal dependencies reach -20 to -40. Must roll vs. Will to resist the urge to use whenever the substance is available.

out.name: Chronic Insomnia
out.notes: Lose 1 FP each morning that cannot be recovered through rest; rolls requiring sustained concentration at -1.

out.name: Class Resentment
out.notes: Must roll vs. Will-2 or express hostility when in prolonged contact with the resented class.

out.name: Compulsive Gambling
out.notes: Regular income loss; prone to debt; requires Will roll at -2 to leave a game while ahead.

out.name: Duty-Bound
out.notes: An obligation takes priority over personal safety. Must regularly sacrifice time, money, or risk to fulfil it.

out.name: Glass Jaw
out.notes: All knockdown rolls from head strikes at -2; concussion effects last longer.

out.name: Glory Hound
out.notes: Must roll vs. Will or ensure your role in any success is publicly known, even when discretion would be wiser.

out.name: Grief-Stricken
out.notes: In situations that echo a specific loss, Will rolls to act clearly are at -2. Can be gradually resolved through play.

out.name: Guilt
out.notes: -1 to Will in situations that echo the original act; may be exploited by people who know the truth.

out.name: Impulsive
out.notes: Must roll vs. IQ-2 to pause and plan; failure means you act on the first reasonable impulse in any urgent situation.

out.name: Reckless
out.notes: -1 to any roll where caution would be smarter; must roll vs. Will to back down from a physical challenge.

out.name: Reputation: Troublemaker
out.notes: Employers, landlords, and officials treat you with pre-emptive suspicion (GM discretion).

out.name: Social Anxiety
out.notes: -2 to social skill rolls in groups of 6+; -3 when addressing strangers of higher status.

out.name: Stubborn
out.notes: Must roll vs. Will-3 to reverse your stated position in the same scene, even when clearly wrong.

out.name: Superstitious (mundane)
out.notes: If warding routine is disrupted, -1 to all rolls for the day; will go out of their way to observe superstitions.

out.name: Reluctant Killer
out.notes: -4 to hit recognizable people with deadly force (-2 if face hidden); cannot Aim. If you kill a recognizable person, become morose for 3d days — Will rolls required to use violence again.

out.name: Cannot Harm Innocents
out.notes: Will not use deadly force when innocent bystanders might be affected, or against enemies not using deadly force on you. Non-deadly force is acceptable.

out.name: Cannot Kill
out.notes: Unwilling to kill anyone, even through omission, or to allow comrades to kill. If responsible for a death, react as Reluctant Killer (-5).

out.name: Self-Defence Only
out.notes: Use violence only to protect yourself or those in your care, to the minimum degree necessary; no pre-emptive strikes.

out.name: Total Non-Violence
out.notes: Will not use violence against intelligent creatures, even in self-defense. May defend against animals.

out.name: Workaholic
out.notes: Cannot relax; always finds something productive to do. -2 to social rolls in leisure settings; rolls to take a day off at Will-3.

out.name: Callous
out.notes: -3 to social skill rolls when warmth or empathy is required. You may still act kindly — but it is an effort and it shows.

out.name: Kleptomania
out.notes: Compelled to steal small objects when the opportunity arises and no consequences are obvious. Roll vs. Will to resist when the situation makes theft easy.

out.name: Skinny
out.notes: -2 to ST for purposes of knockback and grappling; +2 to rolls to escape bonds or fit into tight spaces. Clothing is hard to find off the rack.

out.name: Shyness
out.notes: -1 to -2 to social skill rolls depending on severity and audience. Mild (-5): -1 in groups of 6+; Severe (-10): -2 in groups of 3+.

out.name: Laziness
out.notes: Must roll vs. Will to undertake any sustained effort not immediately necessary or personally interesting. Unemployment is a real risk.

out.name: Clueless
out.notes: -3 to all social skill rolls; generally miss social cues and subtlety. You do not understand subtext, sarcasm, or implication.

out.name: Unfit
out.notes: -1 to all HT rolls; recover FP at half normal rate. Unfit for sustained physical exertion.

out.name: Vow (specify)
out.notes: A solemn promise that restricts your actions. Common examples: Poverty (give away all wealth beyond subsistence) -10, Partial Silence (limited speech) -5, Vegetarian -5.

out.name: Charity
out.notes: Cannot ignore genuine need. Must roll vs. 12 or help anyone who asks for assistance you can reasonably provide. May be exploited.

out.name: Loner
out.notes: Must roll vs. Will to spend extended time in groups larger than 3-4 people. Seek solitude when stressed; -1 to social rolls in crowds.

out.name: Bloodlust
out.notes: Must go for killing blows in combat. IQ roll necessary to accept a surrender or take a prisoner. Downed foes get an extra shot to make sure.

out.name: Weirdness Magnet
out.notes: Strange supernatural events are drawn to you constantly

out.name: Paranoia
out.notes: Must roll vs. 12 or assume strangers are threats; common potion side effect

out.name: Hallucinations
out.notes: Periodic false sensory experiences; visions, voices, phantom presences

out.name: Compulsion (pathway)
out.notes: Uncontrollable urge tied to pathway nature; triggered by stress

out.name: Delusion (minor)
out.notes: Firmly believes something false about the supernatural world

out.name: Coldblooded
out.notes: Morality erodes upon advancement. Roll Will when suppressing evil desires (murder, lust, theft, etc.). Define with the GM which desires apply to your character.

out.name: Compulsive Behavior (Indulge Evil Desires) SC 6
out.notes: When an opportunity to commit an evil act (murder, torture, betrayal, etc.) presents itself, roll 3d6 ≤ 6 or indulge fully. Conscience offers no resistance.

out.name: Aura Leak
out.notes: Spiritual body radiates faintly even suppressed. Beyonders with Spiritual Perception (Ch. 4) detect you automatically within 20 meters.

out.name: Bleed-Through Visions
out.notes: If you have Spirit Vision, it activates involuntarily in emotionally charged locations. Roll vs. Will or be briefly incapacitated by the vision.

out.name: CoR Brand
out.notes: A visible or spiritually legible mark from prior CoR exposure. Church Beyonders who examine you react with suspicion or investigation.

out.name: Dream Invaded
out.notes: Dreams are accessible to outside entities without effort. You are unaware of visitors unless they choose to reveal themselves.

out.name: Ether Body Damage
out.notes: Prior spirit body damage (see Spirit Body Damage, Chapter 5) that never fully healed. All SPI-based rolls at -1; Spirit Vision on you reveals the damage immediately.

out.name: Fate Debt
out.notes: You owe fate something. The GM holds a narrative debt to be called in at a dramatically significant moment. Beckoning Luck never applies.

out.name: Unlucky
out.notes: Once per session the GM may inconvenience you by making your life slightly more difficult. This is a weaker Fate Debt that triggers every session and remains until bought off or resolved through the assistance of a powerful fate-related Beyonder or ritual.

out.name: Pathway Resonance (Hostile)
out.notes: One specific Pathway resonates badly with you (specify). Beings of that Pathway react with instinctive hostility; their abilities against you at +1.

out.name: Residual Contamination
out.notes: Spiritual residue from a forbidden item or ritual. Seers and Spiritual Perception (Ch. 4) users detect 'something wrong' about you.

out.name: Soul Scar
out.notes: Under extreme spiritual stress (Fright Check failure by 5+, witnessing Seq. 5+ abilities), old pain resurfaces: -1 to all rolls for the scene.

out.name: Thinned Veil
out.notes: Boundary between your senses and the spiritual world is unusually permeable. Concentration in spiritually active environments at -2.

out.name: Bound to a Place
out.notes: Spiritually tethered to a location (specify). Leaving for more than one week causes growing unease: -1 to Will per additional week, cumulative.

out.name: Compulsion: Collection (pathway)
out.notes: Compelled to collect specific items (bones, keys, mirrors, etc.). Roll vs. Will-2 when presented with a collectible you do not own.

out.name: Compulsion: Confess
out.notes: Under significant stress, must tell someone a true secret. Roll vs. Will-2 or confess something genuine to the nearest trusted person.

out.name: Compulsion: Preserve the Dead
out.notes: Cannot pass a neglected corpse without properly covering or acknowledging it. Roll vs. Will-3 to continue without addressing them first.

out.name: Drawn to Ritual Sites
out.notes: Pulled toward places where rituals have been performed. When within blocks of a ritual site, compelled to investigate even without obvious reason.

out.name: Evil Eye Fear
out.notes: Avoid eye contact with strangers; periodically perform warding rituals. If interrupted from a warding routine, -1 to Will rolls for the day.

out.name: Honest to Spirits
out.notes: Cannot deliberately lie in the presence of ghosts or entities you know to be spiritually present. Instinctive, not a rational choice.

out.name: Pathway Pull
out.notes: A specific Pathway exerts a narrative pull before you drink a potion. Compelled to follow situations that lead toward it even when wisdom says otherwise.

out.name: Chronophobia (Temporal)
out.notes: Irrational terror of something time-related (clocks stopping, mirrors, specific hours). Triggered: immediate Fright Check at -3.

out.name: Dead-Eyed
out.notes: -2 to first-impression social rolls with strangers; animals are skittish around you; children sometimes cry.

out.name: Unsettling Appearance
out.notes: Your presence instinctively disturbs or repels others — a common consequence of Abyss and Chained Pathway potions. NPCs react with unease or distrust (GM discretion).

out.name: Entity Fixation
out.notes: -1 to all rolls when a specific entity type is present nearby; -2 to any roll that requires you to ignore them.

out.name: Fear of Silence
out.notes: In complete silence — underground, at sea, in empty buildings — must roll vs. Will-2 or feel compelled to speak or make noise.

out.name: Haunted
out.notes: A specific ghost follows you. Other spiritual beings notice it; it may interfere with rituals; can be used as leverage by those who know.

out.name: Memory Bleed
out.notes: Someone else's genuine memories intrude periodically — an unrelated person from your past, or someone whose spiritual body overlapped yours.

out.name: Perceptual Splitting
out.notes: At moments of high spiritual activity, senses temporarily separate from your body. All physical rolls at -2 during an episode (1d seconds).

out.name: Phobia: Sacred Symbols
out.notes: A specific church's symbols, prayers, or holy items cause genuine fright. Fright Check at -2 on direct exposure; -1 in consecrated buildings.

out.name: Spiritually Loud
out.notes: Spiritual presence registers as larger than your actual Sequence would suggest. Perceived as more powerful than you are — a curse as much as a blessing.

out.name: Threshold Blindness
out.notes: One specific entity type or supernatural phenomenon you cannot perceive with any spiritual skill, regardless of roll results (specify at creation).

out.name: Phobia (specify)
out.notes: Irrational fear of a specific thing (cities, spiders, crowds, etc.). Fright Check at -2 when exposed; -1 to all rolls while the phobic stimulus is present and unavoidable. Severity depends on how common the trigger is.

out.definition: The practice of embodying your Beyonder potion's 'role' to digest it safely. The more faithfully you act, the faster you digest (see Digestion).
The layer of a soul that reveals emotional state. Visible through Spirit Vision.
The capital of the Loen Kingdom. A sprawling industrial city of fog, factories, slums, and aristocratic mansions. Most campaigns begin here.
A person who has consumed a potion and gained supernatural abilities along a divine Pathway. Beyonders progress from Sequence 9 (weakest) to Sequence 0 (godlike).

A weapon imbued with spiritual power (either innately or through a Beyonder's ability) that can damage spirit bodies, incorporeal beings, and spiritually reinforced targets as though it were a Beyonder-level effect. Mundane weapons without this property deal half or no damage to such targets at the GM's discretion.

The layer of a soul governing emotion, reason, and self-awareness. Lies between the Astral Body and the Spirit Body. Targeted by Visionary pathway mental manipulation abilities such as Frenzy and Telepathy.
The currency used to build characters. You spend points on attributes, advantages, and skills. Disadvantages give points back. Starting budget: 70 points.
A measure of how close a Beyonder is to losing control. Max CoR = Will score. At max, the character becomes an NPC monster.
Rolling 3–4 is always a critical success (brilliant result). Rolling 17–18 is always a critical failure (disaster).
The process of safely incorporating a potion's power. Tracked as 0% -> 100%. Must be at or near 100% before advancing to the next Sequence.
The outermost layer of a soul, visible through Spirit Vision. Shows physical health — white = healthy, dark = ill.
Energy for physical exertion, extra effort, and some supernatural abilities. Recovered by rest. Equal to HT at character creation.
The player who runs the game — describes the world, plays NPCs, calls for rolls, and keeps the story moving.
Physical damage capacity. Equal to ST at character creation. At 0 HP you are near death; negative HP forces consciousness checks.
See Backlund. The dominant nation of the Fifth Epoch, equivalent to Victorian Britain.
When a Beyonder's CoR reaches their maximum. They transform into a monster or mad creature — permanently removed from play.
The difference between your roll and your target number. A bigger margin means a better (or worse) outcome.
One of 22 divine progressions. Each pathway runs from Sequence 9 to Sequence 0 and grants specific abilities. Examples: Fool Pathway, Error Pathway, Darkness Pathway.
An alchemical brew that grants Beyonder powers. Must be brewed from specific ingredients, then consumed. Brings side effects and corruption risk.
The numerical rank of a Beyonder's power level. Sequence 9 = newly awakened. Sequence 0 = god-equivalent. Lower numbers are stronger.

A spiritual stat (not a buyable attribute). Measures connection to the spirit world. Fixed at 0 for mortals; increased only by Beyonder potions or supernatural means. Used for Spirit Vision, Spiritual Intuition, Spiritual Perception, Ritualistic Magic (as a resource), and Beyonder abilities.

A universal Beyonder ability that reveals auras, Ether Bodies, Astral Bodies, and supernatural entities. Learned as a 10-point advantage (see Chapter 3) or in-game from a teacher once you have 4+ total SPI (see Chapter 4). Costs 1 SPI per activation regardless of duration.
A universal Beyonder ability (see Chapter 4): the soul's early-warning system. Roll 3d6 — the difficulty class is your current SPI (1 SPI needs a critical 3–4; 9 SPI needs 9 or lower).

A universal Beyonder ability (see Chapter 4): acute awareness of the spiritual world — ghosts, auras, traces of magic — that peers into the Astral and Spiritual Bodies of beings. Roll 3d6 — the difficulty class is your current SPI (1 SPI needs a critical 3–4; 9 SPI needs 9 or lower).

A shared psychic realm containing the unconscious minds of all sentient beings. Accessible via certain Visionary-pathway abilities (e.g., Psychological Cue). The GM determines effects when a character enters this realm.
Three six-sided dice rolled together. The standard die roll for all success checks. Add the three numbers for your result (range 3–18).
Mental fortitude and resistance to influence. = IQ at character creation. Used to resist intimidation, mind control, and CoR.

out.text: The world of Loen is linguistically rich. Common languages carry no mystical weight — they are the everyday speech of nations. Mystical languages, by contrast, resonate with the supernatural forces of the Spirit World and are essential for rituals, charms, and Beyonder abilities. Points listed are for Spoken + Written at the given level. Spoken-only or written-only costs half. Language Talent halves all costs (rounded up).
Language Talent (10 pts) halves all language costs. Multilingual (3 pts) grants fluency in two common languages without point cost — it does not apply to mystical languages.

out.effect: Fluent. No penalty to language-dependent skill rolls. Pass as a native speaker.
Noticeable accent. -2 to language-dependent skill rolls.
Simple ideas only. -3 to language-dependent skill rolls. Cannot read complex texts.
Fluent. No penalty. Can perform rituals, read ancient texts, and channel mystical forces through the language.
Functional but imperfect. -2 to language-dependent skill rolls. Rituals using the language at -2.
Recognise common words and phrases. -3 to language-dependent skill rolls. Cannot perform rituals in the language.

out.name: Loen
out.notes: Loen Kingdom — the lingua franca of the Northern Continent

out.name: Feysac
out.notes: Feysac Empire — derived from Ancient Feysac

out.name: Intis
out.notes: Intis Republic — derived from Ancient Feysac

out.name: Balam (Dutan)
out.notes: East and West Balam, Southern Continent — distinct origin from Ancient Feysac but structurally similar

out.name: Highland
out.notes: Mountain regions of the Northern Continent — various dialects

out.name: Rorsted
out.notes: Rorsted Archipelago — derived from Ancient Feysac

out.name: Ancient Hermes
out.notes: Created by the ancient sage Hermes in the Second Epoch, based on Jotun and Dragonese. Direct, powerful — but lacks concealment, making it dangerous for the unprotected. Used for sacrifice and prayer.

out.name: Hermes
out.notes: The improved, safer descendant of Ancient Hermes. Better concealment and protection. Essential knowledge for all Beyonders.

out.name: Elvish
out.notes: Ancient language of the elves. Every word is rich in meaning; sentences are very short. Can shake natural forces. Used for sacrifice, prayer, and spellcasting.

out.name: Dragonese
out.notes: Ancient language of dragons. Can shake natural forces. Used for sacrifice, prayer, and spellcasting.

out.name: Jotun (Giant's)
out.notes: Ancient language of giants. Can shake natural forces. Still in daily use in the City of Silver (Forsaken Land of the Gods). Basis of Ancient Feysac.

out.name: Ancient Feysac
out.notes: Common tongue of the Fourth Epoch and root of all modern Northern Continent languages. Derived from Jotun. Has minor mystical properties but cannot shake natural forces. Considered a mystical language due to its origin and ritual use.

out.effect: -4 to all rolls for 1 turn from shock and pain
Stunned for 1d6 seconds (roll HT each turn to recover early)
Knocked down and unconscious for 1d hours

out.description: Move up to your full Basic Move in meters. May face any direction.
Reload a weapon, draw an item, drink a vial, or prepare equipment.
Add weapon's ACC to your next ranged Attack. +1 per additional Aim (max ACC+2). Canceled by any Active Defense or injury.
If Stunned: -4 to Active Defense. Otherwise rest to recover FP.
Channel powers or skills requiring focus. Roll Will-3 if injured or defending.
Define a trigger; if it occurs, perform your chosen maneuver immediately.
Make one melee or ranged attack. Step 1 meter before or after.
Pay 2 FP. +4 to hit melee, +1 to hit ranged. Cannot defend next turn.
Pay 2 FP. +2 to damage. Cannot defend next turn.
Pay 2 FP. Two separate attacks (roll twice). Cannot defend next turn.
Move full distance, then attack. -4 to hit. Cannot defend next turn.
Pay 2 FP. +2 to one active defense until next turn. Cannot attack.
Pay 2 FP. Use two different defenses vs. one attack. Cannot attack.

Roll a Quick Contest of your Melee skill vs. opponent's Melee, Cloak, Shield, or DX. If you succeed (or succeed by more), subtract your margin of success/victory from their active defense on your next Attack, All-Out Attack, or Move and Attack this turn.

out.ability: Spiritual Dance (1 SPI): Roll Dancing skill to begin a strange, over-the-top dance that places the Dancer in a transcendent, mystical state. After dancing for at least one turn, passively activate Spirit Vision and gain +2 to all Will rolls for 1d turns. Appeasing Dance (2 SPI): Roll Dancing skill at -1. On success, all witnesses must roll Will at -2 or be pacified — rendered calm, non-hostile, and disinclined toward violence for the duration of the dance and 1d turns after. Summoning Dance (4 SPI): Roll Dancing skill at -3, then summon up to 3 spiritual creatures whose powers, temperament, and hostility depend on the quality of the roll. By offering blood to one of them, the Dancer may temporarily have the spiritual creature inhabit their body, gaining the creature's abilities — but suffering severe drawbacks determined by which creature answers (GM's discretion). The creature inhabits the Dancer for 3d turns in combat (roughly 10–30 seconds outside combat). On a critical failure, summon an incredibly hostile spiritual creature that attacks the Dancer immediately, even before the dance ends.
out.advantages: Double-Jointed Ignore up to -5 close-quarters penalties for wrestling or grappling; any body part bends any way
out.name: Dancer

out.ability: Pathogen Mutator (once per day): Roll HT to mutate and empower one of the pathogens inside the Patient's body. On a successful roll, the disease gains +1 level (maximum +3), imposing an additional -1 penalty to HT to resist infection and empowering all of its negative effects. This is displayed as +1 within the disease's stat block — e.g., Flu +1 (Roll HT -1 to not get infected when within 2m of someone infected; -2 to all ST, DX, and HT rolls). Each subsequent use on the same disease increases the level by another +1, up to a maximum of +3. Hyper Contaminator (passive): Any and all of the Patient's bodily fluids are guaranteed to transmit disease. The Patient's pathogens ignore normal methods of transmission — contact, airborne droplets, and environmental vectors all become viable. Even dried or diluted fluids retain full infectious potency.
out.advantages: Hard Stomach Can consume spoiled, rotten, or contaminated food and drink without ill effect; +4 to HT rolls to avoid food-borne illness Resistance (Pathogens) +3 to all HT rolls that involve resisting disease already inside you
out.drawbacks: Pathogen Magnet Perfect host for disease. Upon coming into contact with contaminated material, roll HT -2 or become infected.
out.name: Patient

out.ability: Territory Creation (6 SPI): The Shaman may designate an object as a totem and create a mystical territory around it using Ritualistic Magic. Roll Ritualistic Magic/IQ (Very Hard). Success creates a normal territory (~75m radius); critical success creates an enhanced territory (~150m radius). Failure yields no result. On a critical failure, the Shaman suffers spiritual whiplash and a higher-dimensional monster takes notice of them. Within their territory, the Shaman receives +1 to ST, DX, and HT. Ritualistic Spell Creation (varies): Functionally similar to the Seq 7 Warlock's Spell Creation, the Shaman is able to borrow the powers of spirituality within their domain to create various spells. The specifics must be discussed with the GM, and the spells are always tied to the spirituality found within the territory — e.g., a river's innate spirituality may be used to create a rain spell; a graveyard's spirituality may be used to create a withering spell. All such spells use the Ritualistic Magic/IQ (Very Hard) skill for casting, and they may require inanimate or living sacrifices to activate.
out.drawbacks: Open Soul Due to passively entering an ascended spiritual state, become a target of monsters. Roll 3d at the start of every session; on a critical failure (17-18), attract the attention of a higher-dimensional monster.
out.name: Shaman

out.ability: Fate Sensation (passive): The Dreamless is capable of sensing the flow and changes within fate around them. The GM may call for a Spiritual Intuition roll (3d6, target = current SPI, Ch. 4) to sense specific changes in fate. Fate Sensation (active): At any moment, the Dreamless may concentrate and roll Spiritual Perception (3d6, target = current SPI, Ch. 4) at -2 to sense any nearby changes in fate. This can indicate many things, but all results are restricted to possible fates — absolute certainties or impossibilities lie beyond its reach.
out.drawbacks: Dreamless State Cannot have dreams or receive revelations through them.
out.name: Dreamless

out.ability: Overwhelming Hunger: When doing anything other than searching for food or eating, the Tramp suffers -5 to Will rolls to resist any activity related to duty, compulsion, desire, or goal. Their craving for food takes precedence over nearly everything else.
out.advantages: Enhanced Stomach Penalties related to unfamiliar, rancid, bad-tasting food or other strange substances do not apply. Penalty to emotional damage for eating bad food is not included.
out.drawbacks: Voracious Appetite The Tramp's overwhelming craving for food becomes their primary Desire. The impact of other Desires on them is significantly reduced.
out.name: Tramp

out.drawbacks: Societal Menace A menace to society and a threat to those around you. When other people place trust in you or you sense someone's weakness, you feel a powerful urge to exploit that trust or weakness. Roll Will -4 to resist.
out.name: Villain

out.ability: Greed Inducement (2 SPI): Induces greed into a target, compelling a person to comply with the desire. -2 to the opponent's Will roll, or -4 if an object is used as a medium that the person is greedy for. Ownership: Within 24 hours, the Scrooge can track down the location of an object that belongs to them and find its current location. Gluttony Inducement (2 SPI): Induces a desire to eat something into a target, compelling a person to comply. -2 to the opponent's Will roll, or -4 if the medium is a food the person is hungry for. -1 to the opponent's Will roll if the object designated is inedible.
out.drawbacks: Sin of Greed In any scenario involving spending money, -5 to Will roll to resist (or -1 if it is absolutely necessary). In any scenario involving gaining money, -4 to Will roll — even if the mission is dangerous, the Scrooge accepts it because of their greed.
out.name: Scrooge

out.ability: Order Sense (Passive): The Broker may request the GM to describe the order inclinations of a person, room, conversation, or even something as abstract as an organisation, though appropriate knowledge is required. The GM must answer by describing the shade of 'grey' that is applicable — e.g. "the room appears to be a darker grey" showing the disorderly inclinations of all parties within, "the man appears a radiant, almost pure white" showing incorruptible justice.
out.advantages: Charisma +2 +2 to Influence skills; NPCs predisposed to trust and listen to you
out.drawbacks: Uncertain Order You gain a need to bring all forms of order to 'greyness'. When in a position to transform order or disorder into 'grey', roll against 12 to resist the desire. 'Grey' is the state between order and disorder where uncertainty can be exploited.
out.name: Broker

out.ability: Spell Mastery (Passive): Learn and cast spells through worship of the Inextinguishable Ravings. Midoro's Worship (8 SPI): Roll Ritualistic Magic. Success: learn one spell. Critical success: learn two. Failure: +1 CoR. Critical failure: +3 CoR. Max 3 spells at a time. Learnable spells: Star Scrying (3 SPI): Gaze into the cosmos for a relevant revelation. Passive: once/session roll 3d ≤ 14; better result = better revelation. Failure: +1 CoR. Crit fail: +2 CoR. Eyes of Depravity (2 SPI): All in LOS roll Will-2 or act on base instinct desire for 1d turns. Passive: once/session, Initiator rolls Will-2 or becomes depraved for 1d minutes. Weakening (2 SPI): Target rolls HT-4 or suffers -2 to all rolls for 2d turns. Passive: once/session, Initiator rolls HT-2 or gains -2 to all rolls for 1d minutes. Energize (1 SPI): Target ally or self gains +1 to all rolls for 1d turns. Passive: once/session, Initiator rolls HT-1 or gains -1 to all rolls for 1d minutes. Regeneration (2 SPI per 3 HP): Heal any living thing within 5 m. Up to 6 HP/turn. Passive: once/session, Initiator rolls ST-1 or suffers 5 HP damage. Adrenaline (3 SPI): Target in LOS gains +1 to ST, DX, HT for 2d turns; halve FP costs. Passive: once/session, Initiator rolls HT-2 or loses 5 FP. Earth Wall (4 SPI): Create a 2 m tall, 4 m wide, 20 cm thick wall. Passive: when encountering a pretty plant, roll 12 or stop to admire for 1d minutes. Pulse (3 SPI): Create an impulse from the hands. Anything within 4 m rolls HT/DX/Acrobatics or is knocked down. Passive: once/session, roll HT or suffer headache (-1 IQ rolls) until cured. Sensory Illusion (1 SPI): Create a small sensory illusion to confuse opponents. Passive: once/session, hear a sudden loud sound that distracts. History Replay (4 SPI): Replay the past 12 hours of events in a room. Can fast-forward or start at a specific time.
out.drawbacks: Philosophy Strong desire to contemplate the philosophy of existence. Roll against 12 at any downtime or get lost in deep philosophical introspection.
out.name: Initiator

out.drawbacks: Star Worship At least once per day, roll 3d against 16 to study the cosmos. On a critical failure, gain 1 CoR. On a critical success, gain some insight about the world (up to the GM). If the desire is ignored, after a day gain -1 to all Will rolls (cumulative, per day of non-observing).
out.name: Astronomy Aficionado

out.advantages: Acute Hearing +2 to Hearing rolls; detect faint sounds, eavesdrop through walls, identify speech in noise Wolf of Wall Street +2 to all rolls when representing an organization
out.drawbacks: Compulsion: Corporate Inconvenience When dealing with people while in a position of power, gain a compulsion to make their life harder by overcomplicating the bureaucratic process.
out.name: Secretary

out.ability: Investigation (once per scene): Roll 3d against 14. Depending on the degree of success, the GM must disclose some of the yet undiscovered information about the current scene. Does not necessarily apply only to investigation scenes. On failure, nothing happens. This ability stacks with the Experienced Investigator advantage. True Sight (1 SPI per minute): While active, see through any illusion, substitution, concealment, or other spiritual phenomena at the level of a Sequence higher or below. While active, it is possible for the Reporter to witness the scene from a different angle. For example, if there is a person hiding under a window on the second floor, the Reporter may use True Sight to shift their perspective higher up to see them crouching beneath the window. They may use their Spiritual Intuition to know how to shift their perspective for the best viewing angle.
out.advantages: Acute Vision +2 to vision-based Perception rolls; spot distant details Experienced Investigator +1 to all Investigation, Observation, and Search rolls
out.drawbacks: Imaginary Mismatch Begin to dislike or outright hate anything about the world that does not match your 'fantasy' of how the world should be. Roll against 12 when interacting with a mismatched phenomenon to not show disdain.
out.name: Reporter

out.ability: Painting Hiding (2 SPI): They can hide in some of their Paintings, often taking the form of a human figure. Painting Disguise (2 SPI): They can also use cosmetics on a face to achieve an excellent disguise. This can also be done on someone else. Doesn't need a Disguise roll. Painting Creation (1/2/3 SPI): By using their Spirituality, they can depict the reality they intend, granting their Paintings various Beyonder and mystical effects. A target must stare at a Painting for at least three seconds for its effects to trigger; it can also trigger as an area of effect. Their Paintings are a type of Beyonder Weapon and lose their power over time — about two months when folded and three days when unfolded, at most. The Painting's effect depends on the intent of the Painter and the things painted, with the final result depending on the GM. The Painter must succeed on an Artist (Painting) roll for the Painting to have any effect. They can put more Spirituality into the Painting for a more powerful effect. Painting Manipulation (1 SPI): They can paint a mark onto certain creatures and use the connection between themselves and the Painting to drive the corresponding mark, thereby directing the creature, provided they maintain a certain distance. Costs 1 SPI per additional minute. If the target is of the same or higher Sequence, they can resist with a successful Will roll. Gain a +4 bonus per Sequence of difference.
out.advantages: True Sight Painters see the creative intentions regarding Paintings
out.drawbacks: Mental Instability -1 to Will from Sequence 7 onwards
out.name: Painter

out.ability: Lust Inducement (2 SPI): Induce lust into a target. -2 to the opponent's Will roll, or -4 if a crush or desired type is used as the designated target. Drug Knowledge: Truth Serum: Compels truth-telling. -2 Will (first question), -3 Will (third question), -4 Will (subsequent questions). Cough Antidote Gas: Antidote to Truth Serum. Sedative Gas: ST and DX temporarily reduced to 25% of normal. Hormonal Analysis: Acquire differentiating hormonal information of various individuals.
out.advantages: Fit +1 to all HT rolls; recover FP at twice the normal rate Simp Mental suggestion and charm rolls against you are at -2. From a desired target, these gain +2 (mental suggestion) or +4 (charm).
out.drawbacks: Sin of Lust Replaces Sin of Greed. Crave intimate acts with another person. -5 to Will when pursuing, performing, or preparing for the deeds.
out.name: Sex Addict
out.reinforcedAbilities: Greed Inducement: The Sex Addict's Sin-based compulsion may be substituted for Greed Inducement — treat as Greed Inducement with -3 to the target's Will (instead of -2). If a desired object or person is used as the medium, the penalty increases to -5 (from -4). Ownership: The Sex Addict can track any person they have had intimate contact with within the past 48 hours (from 24 hours). The tracking is instinctive — no roll required unless the target is shielded by anti-divination wards (roll Spiritual Intuition, 3d6, target = current SPI, to bypass). Gluttony Inducement: Can now induce cravings beyond food — alcohol, drugs, or any consumable substance. The Will penalty increases by +1 in all cases (-3 base, -5 if the consumable is already desired).

out.ability: Luck Intuition (Passive): Without a roll, the Alms Monk understands the luck of any person within line of sight. They perceive a vague trend through different colours (e.g. future romantic encounter, possible wealth gain, impending life-threatening calamity). The exact nature is up to the GM. Prophecy Spell (3 SPI): After gathering several ingredients (not too rare), combine them into a concoction and feed it to a non-purified corpse that has been dead for less than a week. After completing the ritual, ask 3 questions about the future of anyone or anything. The GM must provide true answers within reason. Questions regarding demigods always fail. The prophecy answers only one element per question (if a question has multiple elements — e.g. "when and where" — only one is answered). Luck Enhancement Spell (3 SPI): The Alms Monk can 'extract' someone else's bad luck using a mystical medium (such as blood, or their own) and attach it to an object. If that object is opened, taken, worn, or stepped on without the Alms Monk's explicit or implied consent, the bad luck transfers to that individual. If the luck is not transferred within 3 days of attachment, the bad luck returns and becomes untransferable for a month. Animal Creation Spell (3 SPI): The Alms Monk can enchant a full animal skin. After covering a person with it, it allows them to turn into that animal with an incantation, and a separate incantation to return. The animal skin must be large enough to fully cover the person. After use, it loses its mystical properties but may be used for the creation of a new pelt. Exorcism Spell (4 SPI): By knowing a wraith's or spectre's true name, the Alms Monk rolls Ritualistic Magic vs. the spirit's SPI or Will (whichever is higher). On success, the creature is exorcised. The ritual requires at least 5 turns to take effect.
out.advantages: Resistant (Weather) +8 to HT vs. weather hazards
out.name: Alms Monk
out.reinforcedAbilities: Spiritual Dance: The Alms Monk may substitute a slow, meditative walk for the dance. The +2 to Will rolls extends to all SPI-based rolls and lasts for 2d turns (from 1d). For an Alms Monk who has learned Spirit Vision (Ch. 4), it activates automatically at no SPI cost while the walk continues. Appeasing Dance: The Will penalty for witnesses increases to -4 (from -2). The Alms Monk may target a single hostile creature with the appeasing effect without needing to perform the full dance — a gesture and a murmured verse suffice (costs 1 SPI, range 10 m). Summoning Dance: On a successful summon, the Alms Monk may negotiate with the summoned creature for an additional service (beyond inhabitation) — the creature will perform one task of equivalent difficulty to the summoning, provided the task aligns with its nature. The creature remains for up to 1 hour outside combat (instead of 10-30 seconds).

out.ability: Fate Symphony (passive): Fate Sensation is enhanced. The Musician constantly hears the symphony of fate around them. Symphony Decryption (active): Concentrate on a source and roll IQ to decrypt its symphony. Success reveals several possible futures. Critical success yields a clear sign. On failure, spend 1 FP. On critical failure, spend 3 FP and gain 1 CoR. What the Musician discerns depends on the degree of success and GM discretion. Song of Fate (varies): After decrypting a target's fate, the Musician may amplify it by singing. Roll Singing (HT/Easy) with a bonus or penalty depending on the significance of the fate amplified (GM discretion). Spend SPI appropriate to the effect (GM discretion). The Musician may spend additional SPI to forcibly succeed on the Singing roll. Fate cannot be changed — only amplified. Examples: amplifying the fate of an impending illness forces the target to roll HT or fall ill immediately; amplifying the fate of an emotional breakdown forces a Will roll or the target becomes uncontrollable temporarily.
out.drawbacks: Distracted by Sight When not blinded or wearing a blindfold, −2 to Symphony Decryption and Song of Fate.
out.name: Musician

out.ability: Shadow Creature Detection (1 SPI): Detect any shadow creature within vicinity. If possible for one to be nearby, the GM must determine the power and hostility of the shadow creature. If the creature is of a sufficiently high level, roll Will or gain 1 CoR upon witnessing it. Due to Pacifying Aura it is possible for the Shadow Merchant to broker deals with these creatures. When dealing with shadow creatures, it is prudent not to show malice, attack them, or secretly plot against them. Shadow Contract (4 SPI): Form contracts with any consenting party, with each other's shadows acting as witnesses. The other party must possess a shadow or be a shadow creature for the contract to be binding. At signing the Shadow Merchant can roll Will to bend the contract's terms, with the degree of success indicating how much can be distorted (up to the GM). If broken by either party, the responsible party receives 2d+1 spiritual damage. Fake Shadow Creation (Varies): Create fake shadows within a 10 m area. Shadow Transformation (3 SPI per 10 min): Transform into shadows and move through them at Base Speed × 4. By transforming into a shadow the Shadow Merchant can avoid most forms of physical damage by rolling against DX +3. Shadow Concealment (1 SPI per 10 min): Conceal themselves in shadows. Roll Per -3 to detect them while still, Per -1 while moving. Attacking or sudden actions break concealment.
out.advantages: Pacifying Aura Unless provoked, anyone with malice towards you rolls Will -4 or becomes pacified. Disadvantage decreased or turned into advantage depending on the being's level, up to the GM
out.name: Shadow Merchant

out.ability: Consciousness Understanding (Passive): By rolling Psychology -2, the Commentator can glean significantly more information about a person, similar to a Spectator's analysis. Commentary (2 SPI): Roll an appropriate speech skill at -2. All who hear the Commentator must roll Will against the Commentator's degree of success on their speech roll, or become influenced by their ideas.
out.name: Commentator
out.reinforcedAbilities: Midoro's Worship: The Commentator can now hold up to four spells at a time (up from three).

out.ability: Danger Intuition: Passive. The Seer intuitively detects lethal danger nearby using Spirituality. The GM provides a vague warning sense whenever mortal danger is near — no roll required.
out.advantages: Eidetic Memory continuously grows as the potion digests; allows memorisation of complex ritual steps and divination methods
out.name: Seer

out.ability: Treasure Sense: The Marauder can sense the presence of valuable items within a 10-meter range — coins, jewellery, artifacts, hidden pouches — but cannot determine their exact location or what they are. The sense is a vague pull: stronger for higher value, weaker for trinkets. At the GM's discretion, unusually powerful or ancient items may register as a distinct "weight" in the perception.
out.name: Marauder

out.ability: Door Opening (1 SPI): Apprentices can open things related to Doors. Any mundane lock, bolt, latch, or physical door can be opened by touch. Using the unique traits of the Spirit World, an Apprentice can phase through walls and other big obstacles by Opening a symbolic, incorporeal Door but cannot bring others through or see through. This extends to doors on the human body: an Apprentice may touch a wound, a joint, or a bodily passage by will — treated as an attack dealing 2d6 cut damage that bypasses mundane armor. Make a Brawling roll or a DX-based touch attack to land it on a resisting target.
out.name: Apprentice

out.ability: Body Language Analysis (1 FP): Spectators use their powers of keen observation to analyze people's expressions, manners, and subconscious actions. For groups of people, this may reveal their surface-level thoughts and dominant emotions — what they are feeling right now and what is occupying their mind. This is surface only; deep intentions, lies of omission, and suppressed feelings are not automatically revealed. On a singular target, roll Psychology to deduce and form a mental model of the target. At the GM's discretion, learn more detailed information about a target's current thoughts and emotions depending on factors such as: the margin of success, how powerful the target is, time spent observing them, prior information known about them, etc. Any target who is sharp perceptively (Per 13+) can roll Per to notice the Spectator observing them. Success by 0–4: they notice something is observing them. Success by 5+ or Critical Success: they also identify the source of where and what is observing them.
out.advantages: Acute Vision +2 to Vision rolls Eidetic Memory +5 to remember things after one reading; near-perfect recall
out.name: Spectator

out.ability: Singing — Buff Effects: Through Singing, a Bard imbues effects onto themselves and nearby allies. On a successful Singing roll (no penalty), the Bard selects ONE of the following effects for all allies within earshot for 10 minutes: (a) Courage — allies ignore Fright Check penalties up to -3; (b) Strength — allies gain +1 to ST-based rolls; (c) Agility — allies gain +1 to DX-based rolls; (d) Spiritual Recovery — allies recover 1 SPI at the song's end (Bard cannot benefit from this effect). No SPI cost — the Bard's voice itself carries the power. At Sequence 9 a Bard cannot produce effects beyond these through Singing.
out.advantages: Fit +1 to all HT rolls; recover FP at twice the normal rate
out.name: Bard

out.ability: Phantom Scales (passive): Illusory scales beneath the skin grant DR 1 vs. physical impacts. Anyone grappling or grabbing the Sailor rolls at -2 (slippery as a fish). Aquatic Affinity — Diving: Without equipment the Sailor freely submerges and acts underwater for at least 10 minutes, diving to at least 15 meters without protection. Ignore all underwater movement penalties; hold breath 10 minutes without a roll; dive to 15 m without HT rolls.
out.advantages: Perfect Balance +6 avoid knockdown; +2 Acrobatics, Climbing, Piloting
out.name: Sailor

out.ability: Reading — Knowledge Wealth: A Reader's comprehension is exceptional. All study, research, and reading is completed in half the normal time — books, scrolls, and languages are absorbed twice as fast, and the Reader learns new languages in half the normal time.
out.advantages: Eidetic Memory +5 to remember things after one reading; near-perfect recall
out.name: Reader

out.ability: Knowledge (Honorifics): Knowledge gained from the potion includes honorific names for secret existences. Three-part honorific learned: "The Lord that Created Everything; The Lord who Reigns Behind the Curtain of Shadows; The Degenerate Nature of all Living Things." Another three-part honorific: "The Lingering Hero Spirit of The River; The Eyes that Look at Fate; The Great Soothsayer of Past, Present, and Future."
out.drawbacks: Paranoia, Hallucinations, or Compulsion (Hanged Man; -10 pts) Choose one of these three drawbacks. Paranoia: you trust no one, always suspect betrayal. Hallucinations: you see and hear things that are not there. Compulsion (Hanged Man): an irresistible urge to seek out secrets and hidden knowledge, even when dangerous.
out.name: Secrets Supplicant

skills.name: Ritualistic Magic
skills.note: — decent knowledge of rituals, especially sacrifices

out.ability: Nocturnality (passive): +1 to all rolls during the night. Danger Detection in the Dark: Passive Danger Sense that is specifically heightened in low-light and dark environments (+2 to the roll when in darkness). In any darkness the Sleepless navigates without penalty and suffers no night-based Perception penalty.
out.advantages: Reduced Sleep Requires only 3–4 hours of rest per day; otherwise functions as Does Not Sleep
out.name: Sleepless

out.ability: Undead Deterrence: Mindless undead/spirits (IQ 5−) with SPI ≤ yours ignore you unless provoked. Intelligent (IQ 6+) or controlled undead may roll Will to act against you. Controlled undead roll at −2; intelligent undead roll without penalty. No effect on undead with SPI > yours or created by Seq 5+ Beyonders. Undead Detection: Corpse Collectors naturally detect undead and spirit creatures within 15 meters without rolling. They understand the characteristics and weaknesses of many undead beings. Observation rolls to understand undead beings are at +3.
out.advantages: Cold Resistance No penalties from cold environments; hypothermia rolls at +2 Resistant (Decay and Corrosiveness) HT rolls to resist corrosiveness (acid, rust) and decay effects at +3
out.drawbacks: Fear of Sunlight and Purification −1 to Will, skills, and combat actions under strong holy/purified/sunlight effects. Must roll Will to approach their source. Sunlight/purification/holy attacks gain +1 against you.
out.name: Corpse Collector

out.ability: Combat Mastery (Passive): The Warrior has mastery of all kinds of weapons and armour, with no weapon they cannot use and no fighting style they cannot learn. The Warrior suffers no default penalty when using any weapon type for the first time — every weapon is treated as known at effective DX (no default penalty) from the moment it is picked up. Weapons used repeatedly in a session are treated as known at default +2. Example: A Warrior who picks up a flintlock pistol for the first time fires it at DX level immediately, but needs several shots before reaching full proficiency (default +2 after repeated use). They also don and maintain any armour type without penalty and fight effectively in it regardless of prior experience.
out.name: Warrior

out.ability: Feather Fall: Assassins can descend from any height without injury. All falls are treated as controlled regardless of height — the Assassin always lands safely and silently. While descending they may glide short horizontal distances (up to 1 meter horizontal per 2 meters vertical). Not sustained flight; cannot maintain altitude. Lands without audible impact — no Perception roll detects the landing through sound alone. Shadow Concealment: The Assassin's body instinctively blends with shadows. In any environment with partial shadow or dim lighting, the Assassin is supernaturally difficult to notice — observers must succeed at a Perception roll at -3 to detect them while they are stationary, and at -1 while moving slowly. This is a passive physical change, not a trained skill. Bright, open daylight negates this effect. Mighty Blow (3 FP): Spend 3 FP and roll the appropriate melee skill. You gain +3 to hit. On a hit, multiply raw damage dice by 3 (before DR). This ability cannot be modified by other maneuvers or by burning FP.
out.advantages: Night Vision see in total darkness without penalty Acute Vision +2 to vision-based Perception rolls Acute Hearing +2 to hearing-based Perception rolls
out.name: Assassin

out.ability: Environment Memory: Hunters have an unwavering memory for any alterations made to their surroundings. Any previously visited location is perfectly recalled, and the Hunter automatically notices any alteration to a visited location. Natural traps — unstable cliffs, quicksand, deadfall zones — are detected instinctively without any roll. Survival Knowledge: The Hunter possesses innate knowledge of wild plants and animal organs, including which plants and organs serve as hemostatic agents when injured and which can be rendered into poisons to coat weapons. Identifying and preparing these requires no roll in wilderness environments. Hemostatic poultices prepared this way restore 1d HP to a bleeding wound (requires 1 minute and a First Aid roll at +2); if not bleeding, they restore 2 HP. Only one such poultice per injury per character.
out.advantages: Acute Vision +2 to vision-based Perception rolls; spot distant details Acute Hearing +2 to hearing-based Perception rolls; detect faint sounds Danger Sense (partial) warning sense for immediate physical danger — less reliable for non-physical threats
out.name: Hunter

out.ability: Eyes of Mystery Prying (1 SPI/min): A Mystery Pryer's eyes are special and allow them to see things that are normally invisible. Always-on passive effects: peer through attempts to trap them in Dreams or Illusions (all such rolls against them are at -2). Active use — expend 1 SPI and roll SPI — to activate Spirit Vision: detect if something is a Mystical Item or if someone is a Beyonder via their Astral Projection, and to examine the full state of a target's Astral Body, Ether Body, and Body of Heart and Mind: reveals injury, spiritual corruption, active Beyonder abilities, and potion side effects. Corruption Exposure: When actively prying into a target who has 5+ CoR, a sealed evil artefact, or an eldritch entity, the Mystery Pryer must make an immediate Will roll or gain 1 CoR from witnessing things the mind was not meant to see. The GM may call for additional Will rolls whenever the Pryer glimpses truly forbidden knowledge. Spirit Contract (Ritual): The Mystery Pryer gains knowledge of the Spirit World Creature Contract ritual (Section VI, Chapter 9). The Mystery Pryer's training delays the per-contract penalty: the 1d6 per-contract roll does not apply until their 2nd contracted creature (1st contract is free, 2nd starts the 1d6 scaling). Base difficulty still equals their Sequence number. Quick Rituals: The penalty for rushed rituals is decreased by 3.
out.drawbacks: Knowledge Pursuit Flat 3d6 roll under 14 — GM decides what information you uncover. On failure, gain 1 CoR. On critical failure, gain 3 CoR instead. Knowledge revealed is at the GM's discretion and may include honorific names, partial/full potion formulas, spirit summoning incantations, spells, curses, mystical and non-mystical ingredients, and more.
out.name: Mystery Pryer

out.ability: Recall — Total Memory: The Savant can recall every piece of knowledge and experience they have ever encountered. No roll is required — it simply works at any time. Additionally, the Savant understands the operation of any mechanism, construct, or device within 1 minute of examination (IQ roll, no penalty) rather than the usual 1 hour. Rapid Analysis: improvised devices and repairs take half the normal construction time.
out.name: Savant

out.ability: Foresight: A Monster is able to hear or see things that others cannot. Occasionally they gain glimpses of the future — this is the specialty of the Wheel of Fortune Pathway, allowing them to perceive things that even Pathways with strong Spirit Vision abilities cannot see. Once per session the Monster receives a spontaneous, unbidden vision of something about to happen (the GM provides a brief cryptic image or impression). This cannot be triggered on demand — it arrives when fate deems it relevant. Danger Premonition: Passive Danger Sense that specifically includes premonitions of bad luck and fate-based traps, not only immediate physical violence.
out.drawbacks: Monster Trance The Monster occasionally enters a trance-like state (GM's discretion), usually triggered by strong fate currents or significant future events. During a trance, the Monster is unaware of their surroundings and vulnerable.
out.name: Monster

out.ability: Farming Tools Proficiency: When fighting with a farming tool, the Planter chooses the most appropriate skill and gains +2 to the attack roll. For example, a shovel would use either the Mace skill or the Polearm skill (GM's decision based on how it is wielded).
out.name: Planter

out.ability: Potion Concoction: The Apothecary can brew a variety of alchemical concoctions. Each potion requires appropriate ingredients (GM discretion on rarity and cost) and a Pharmacy roll at the listed penalty. An Apothecary may carry up to (SPI) doses of prepared potions at any time. Multiple doses of the same potion count separately.  Libido Potion (Pharmacy -1): Powdered mummy and aromatic herbs. The drinker gains exceptional stamina and drive for up to 12 hours. Typically used recreationally or socially; creative players may find other uses.  General Physical Enhancer (Pharmacy -2): Common medicinal herbs, rabbit's foot, honeysuckle extract (or any Seq 9 supplementary ingredient besides liquor). Grants +1 to ST, HT, DX, and Basic Speed for 5 minutes. After the duration expires, the user loses 1/3 of their remaining FP (round up) and their FP maximum is halved (round up) until they sleep for at least 8 hours. If current FP exceeds the new cap, it is reduced to match.  Minor Healing Potion (Pharmacy -1, any character with Pharmacy skill): Common herbs and clean bandages. Heals 1d-1 HP (minimum 1) immediately. Stops active bleeding. Takes 1 minute to prepare. Cost: £1 per dose. Non-Apothecaries can make this with basic first aid knowledge.  Moderate Healing Potion (Pharmacy -3, requires Apothecary skill): Medicinal herbs, honey, and mineral salts. Heals 2d-2 HP (minimum 1) immediately. Cures one minor condition (minor burn, mild infection, light poison). Takes 5 minutes to prepare. Cost: £5 per dose. Requires Apothecary skill to brew properly.  Major Healing Potion (Pharmacy -5, requires Apothecary skill): Rare herbs and spiritual animal parts costing approximately £20 per dose. Heals 3d-3 HP (minimum 1) immediately. Cures one serious condition (deep wound infection, moderate poison, broken bone). Stabilises critical patients. Takes 10 minutes to prepare. Requires Apothecary skill; improper brewing risks minor Toxic damage (1d-2).  Specialised Physical Enhancer (Pharmacy -3): Requires 3 different supplementary ingredients plus a specific base liquid. Grants +3 to a single attribute for 3 minutes, determined by the base liquid: hard liquor → ST, soft liquor (wine, etc.) → HT, water → DX. After the duration expires, the user loses 1/3 of their remaining FP (round up) and their FP maximum is halved (round up) until they sleep for at least 8 hours. If current FP exceeds the new cap, it is reduced to match.  Energy Potion (Pharmacy -1): Sugar, honey, coffee powder, and energising herbs. Reduces the user's maximum FP by 1/4 (round up) and instantly restores their FP to the new maximum. Example: 1 FP out of 12 → max reduced by 3 to 9, user now has 9 FP. Each subsequent use further reduces maximum FP by 1/4 of the current maximum. Lost maximum FP returns after 8 hours of uninterrupted sleep.
out.advantages: Poison Resistance +3 to all HT rolls against poison and toxic substances
out.name: Apothecary

out.ability: Criminal Proficiency — Universal Weapons: Regardless of the weapon — knightly sword, dagger, longbow, pistol, rifle, machine gun, or a spoon — they can utilise all of them to kill a target effectively. The Criminal treats any improvised weapon as their Knife or Brawling skill (whichever is appropriate). They are equally deadly with ranged weapons as with melee — a Criminal can pick up any firearm and fire it with ease, using the most similar Gun skill available.
out.drawbacks: Criminal's Mind Roll Will when suppressing evil desires. Define with the GM which new evil desires define your character — murder, lust, theft, etc.
out.name: Criminal

out.ability: Knowledge — Criminal Expert: Upon advancement, Prisoners gain knowledge that makes them masters of many criminal techniques: picking locks with wire, digging tunnels with improvised tools, and killing with seemingly harmless items. Improvised weapons suffer no penalties and are treated as Brawling or ST. Escape rolls against mundane confinement suffer no penalty or disadvantage regardless of the restraint type. The Prisoner also has an instinctive awareness of confinement — they always know within a 10-meter range if a space has a hidden exit or concealed mechanism even before searching (the GM reveals information regarding this).
out.advantages: Binding (Prisoner) Spirituality and desires are Bound; Spiritual Perception (Ch. 4) and readings of Ether Body and Astral Projection against them are at -4 when composed. Ether Body and Astral Projection appear indistinct and calm, making it difficult to detect you are a Beyonder. When not composed or actively indulging, this trait is temporarily lost.
out.drawbacks: Turbulent Heart Roll Will when suppressing desires. Define with the GM which new strong desires define your character — knowledge, lust, murder, etc.
out.name: Prisoner

out.ability: Authority (1 SPI): Arbiters possess a convincing charm and considerable authority, causing people to be more likely to believe and obey their commands and words. Spend 1 SPI to activate for the scene. When in conflict against an Arbiter, opponents waver — any NPC opposing the Arbiter in combat or social conflict must succeed at a Will roll (no modifier) or suffer -1 to attack rolls, defense rolls, and Quick Contests of Will against the Arbiter for the duration of the scene (or until they leave earshot). On a critical failure, the penalty increases to -2. Player characters who fail the Will roll feel a strong pull to comply but are never mechanically forced — the choice remains theirs.
